paragraph:
This is an automated hazard-exposure briefing produced by Riprap from live and baked data sources. It is informational only and not a substitute for a professional risk assessment.

**Answer.**
801 Father Capodanno Boulevard, Staten Island, was recorded within the empirical 2012 Hurricane Sandy inundation footprint (NYC OEM) [sandy_inundation].

**Hazard Reader.**
This address sits within the empirical 2012 Hurricane Sandy inundation footprint (NYC OEM) [sandy_inundation]. This address sits in FEMA flood zone AE (a Special Flood Hazard Area), per NFHL FIRM panel 3604970329F, effective 2007 [fema_nfhl]. This address is outside the modeled flooding in the NYC DEP stormwater scenario (2.13 in/hr, 2050 SLR) [dep_moderate_2050].

**Live Observer.**
2 FloodNet community sensor(s) within 600 m have logged 37 above-curb flood event(s) in the last 3 years. Peak depth recorded by these sensors: 408 mm [floodnet]. 7 NYC 311 flood-related complaints were filed within 200 m of this location in the last 5 years. Most common descriptor: Sewer Backup (Use Comments) (SA) [nyc311].

**Out of scope.** This briefing does not assess title, structural condition, or compliance with specific zoning rules. Where a probe was offline at run time, the relevant section omits that signal.
